battle.title: Page Table Pit Stop
battle.description: Translate addresses, dodge fragmentation and race the TLB.

questions.text: Compared with contiguous allocation, what does paging do about fragmentation?
options: It removes internal and external fragmentation
It removes external fragmentation but can waste space in a process's last page
It removes internal fragmentation but causes external fragmentation
It has no effect on fragmentation
questions.answer: It removes external fragmentation but can waste space in a process's last page
questions.explanation: Any free frame can hold any page, so scattered free frames are all usable and there is no external fragmentation. A process rarely fills its final page exactly, which leaves internal fragmentation.

questions.text: A system uses 4096-byte pages. What does this program print for the logical address?
questions.explanation: Page number = address / page size = 20000 / 4096 = 4 (integer division). Offset = address % page size = 20000 - 4 * 4096 = 3616. Rounding up to page 5 is the common mistake.

questions.text: What does the TLB (translation lookaside buffer) cache?
options: Recently used page-table entries (page to frame translations)
Recently used data blocks from main memory
Pages that were swapped out to disk
questions.answer: Recently used page-table entries (page to frame translations)
questions.explanation: A TLB hit avoids an extra memory access to read the page table. Caching actual data blocks is the job of the CPU data cache, which is a different structure.

questions.text: A 64-bit process uses only a few small regions of its huge virtual address space. A flat page table per process would be enormous. What is the standard remedy?
options: Keep one flat table and store it only on disk
Disable virtual memory for that process
questions.explanation: A multi-level table only allocates second-level tables for regions actually in use, so unused address space costs almost nothing. A 1-byte page would make the table even larger.

questions.text: A process touches a valid page that is not currently in RAM. Which sequence describes what happens?
options: The process is killed with a segmentation fault
The OS ignores it and returns zeros
The OS loads the page into a frame, updates the page table and restarts the instruction
The OS copies the whole process to disk and restarts it
questions.answer: The OS loads the page into a frame, updates the page table and restarts the instruction
questions.explanation: This is a page fault: the page is legal but not resident, so the OS fetches it from disk (evicting another page if no frame is free) and retries. A segfault happens only for an illegal access.
